subject: Planning sprint: targets & contingency planning
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Planning sprint: targets & contingency planning

Team —

Kicking off annual planning "sprint" for Q1 targets and contingency scenarios. Goal is to land firm target ranges and a clear contingency playbook we can execute if macro or capacity signals shift. High level ask: please review the attached starter workbook (2026_q1_budget_scenarios.xlsx) and provide line-item target proposals by end of day Monday, Sep 27.

Proposed timeline (rough):
- Sep 27: Targets submitted (by functional owner)
- Sep 29: Scenario workshop (2 hrs) — Base / Conserv / Aggressive and corresponding capacity/cost triggers
- Oct 4: Leadership sync (30 min) to agree steer for Q1 commit

Key items to include in your submissions: 1) Revenue/usage targets by product route (hosted API, Dedicated, Private), 2) Cost assumptions (infra + S&M + headcount), 3) Contingency triggers and rollback plans (e.g., burst limits, fallback model flavors), 4) Any external dependencies (market, partnerships).

Attachments: 2026_q1_budget_scenarios.xlsx (starter numbers), planning-playbook-v1.pdf (agenda + roles).

If you think another person should be on the thread for a particular ask, call it out in your reply. I expect Laura to lead the baseline finance numbers; Marcus to flag infra constraints; Lauren to coordinate GTM levers. Sergio — please confirm capacity planning ownership and whether you want Ops on the workshop invite.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Planning sprint: targets & contingency planning

On Mon, Sep 20, 2026 at 09:02, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Kicking off annual planning "sprint" for Q1 targets and contingency scenarios...

Thanks Jonas — clear ask. A couple quick notes from GTM:
- Please ensure GTM targets include both new logos and expansion ARR by product route. We need separate breakout for self-serve vs. sales-assisted flows.
- For contingency, let's adopt simple trigger bands tied to 7-day active request volume and cost-per-1k tokens. If cost per 1k goes above X for more than 3 days we default to conservative model routing.
- Can Marcus include an engineering cost delta table (quantization, batching, infra) in the workbook? That will make trade-offs explicit.

I'll capture initial GTM target proposals by Sep 27. Sergio — can you confirm whether Ops will attend the Sep 29 workshop?

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Growth & GTM

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Rogers <ava.rogers@buttonlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:15:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning sprint: targets & contingency planning

Jonas / team —

I pulled together a first-pass baseline in the attached workbook (tab: FIN_BASELINES). Highlights:
- Baseline revenue split (hosted:dedi:private) = 55:30:15 for Q1; preliminary ARR target +9% vs. last year for Base.
- Three scenarios included: Base / Downside (-8%) / Upside (+18%). Each scenario includes modeled COGS, infra, and a preliminary hiring plan (headcount delta by function).

Open asks for the group:
1) Marcus — I need realistic infra unit costs for the conservative model (quantized instances, cold-start penalties) by EOD Wed so I can lock the Downside P&L.
2) Lauren — confirm whether we should treat marketplace partner revenue as 50% gross or full pass-through for Q1 modeling.
3) Jonas — would like clarity on the contingency cadence — is it automated thresholds or monthly reviews? My preference is a hybrid: automated alerting with a weekly leadership gating call if thresholds are hit.

Attachment: 2026_q1_budget_scenarios.xlsx (FIN_BASELINES tab).

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 16:02:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning sprint: targets & contingency planning

Laura / team —

Quick note on infra assumptions: the conservative Downside bucket in the workbook is optimistic around request-latency sensitive routes. If we assume 10% higher tail latency under load, cost to keep 95th p95 latency targets rises ~12-15% due to overprovisioning and more frequent fallback to higher-memory model variants.

I'm attaching a short runbook excerpt in the Drive link below with the tuning knobs I'm referencing. My recommendation: build a 10% buffer into the Downside infra line, and explicitly model a "degraded mode" routing policy (quantized fallback + lower concurrency) that preserves availability but reduces throughput by ~20% — that will be our action when the 7-day cost-per-1k token crosses the threshold Lauren suggested.

Drive excerpt: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleDriveLink (see file: infra-playbook/contingency-runbook.md)

I'll update the infra tab in the workbook with revised numbers by EOD Wed.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Engineering — Serving Runtime

Great progress — thank you. Quick wrap and next steps: 

Decisions / actions agreed:
- Baseline numbers (Laura) accepted for workshop prep. Laura — we'll treat marketplace partner revenue as gross for modeling unless GTM flags material variance by Sep 27.
- Contingency approach: hybrid (automated alerts + weekly leadership gate). Marcus to bake the degraded-mode routing policy and a 10% buffer into the Downside infra tab.
- GTM will split targets into new logos vs expansion and submit by Sep 27 (Lauren).

Deliverables due Sep 27 (owners):
- Laura: FIN_BASELINES locked + consolidated P&L (attachment already in progress).
- Marcus: infra costs + degraded-mode numbers (will update workbook).
- Lauren: GTM target sheet (self-serve vs sales-assisted).

I'll schedule the Sep 29 scenario workshop invite for 2:00–4:00pm PT and include Ops and CS for run-throughs. Please upload final workbooks and any supporting decks to the Drive folder (link below) and flag anything you need from Finance (Laura) or external consultant Kirsten before EOD Sep 27.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleDriveLink
